study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Pinaya et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2018
study_identification_part.si4_title: Using deep autoencoders to identify abnormal brain structural patterns in neuropsychiatric disorders: A large-scale multi-sample study

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract clearly states the study's aim to build a normative model using a deep autoencoder trained on healthy controls and to estimate total and regional neuroanatomical deviations in patients with schizophrenia and autism spectrum disorder. This directly articulates the research questions and the purpose of applying normative modeling (to quantify deviations and characterize disease-related patterns).
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "We used an artificial neural network known as 'deep autoencoder' to create a normative model using structural magnetic resonance imaging data from 1,113 healthy people. We then used this model to estimate total and regional neuroanatomical deviation in individual patients with schizophrenia and autism spectrum disorder..."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study builds a new normative model using healthy controls from the HCP dataset. It specifies the data source and final sample size (1,113 HC) and restricts clinical datasets to the same age range (22–37) for comparability. However, explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria for the HCP reference cohort, image quality/completeness standards, and reasons for exclusion are not described within the article; detailed acquisition info is deferred to supporting information of the datasets.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The data used in this study were obtained from three public data sets: Human Connectome Project (HCP)..."; "we used sMRI data from 1,113 healthy controls taken from the '1200 Subjects Data Release'..."; "From these two clinical data sets, we identified and selected those subjects within the same age range of the HCP data set (from 22 to 37 years old)."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex are considered via a semi-supervised branch predicting these variables during training and by restricting clinical cohorts to match the HCP age range. However, there is no description of handling multi-site effects (e.g., site covariate, harmonization) despite using multi-sample data.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "During the training, the deep autoencoder learns to reconstruct the input data and to predict the observed variables y, in this case, the subject's age and sex."; "we identified and selected those subjects within the same age range of the HCP data set (from 22 to 37 years old)."
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.location: Pinaya2019.pdf.md: Fig.1 caption context (line 81); Methods 2.2 Subjects (line 71)

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing software (FreeSurfer v5.3.0) and steps (recon-all, Desikan–Killiany parcellation, whole-brain segmentation; extraction of cortical thickness and volumes) are described. Quality control procedures are not described.

For the NUSDAST and ABIDE data sets, we used the same FreeSurfer pipeline (version 5.3.0) ... using the 'recon-all' command ... parcellated according to the Desikan–Killiany atlas ... whole brain segmentation procedure."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The study performs K-fold cross-validation on the HCP reference cohort to select the autoencoder configuration and reports validation performance metrics.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "We executed a cross-validation process on the HCP data to determine the best number of neurons ... mean reconstruction error of 0.40 ± 0.01 ... age prediction MAE ... sex prediction balanced accuracy ..."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The trained normative model is applied to independent external datasets (NUSDAST and ABIDE), including their healthy control groups, demonstrating generalization beyond the training data.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "we applied the trained model to the others data sets ... mean deviation metric of 0.97 ± 0.23 for the HC group ... (NUSDAST) ... 1.09 ± 0.30 for the HC group ... (ABIDE)."
